{
  "question_intent": "Inquiries about USCB's capital allocation and growth plan, specifically regarding Best Egg and deposit business within BUK.",
  "main_topics": ["USCB capital allocation", "Best Egg growth plan", "Deposit business in BUK"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",

  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "Two questions from me. One again, just on Best Egg, but just more in terms of USCB capital allocation and growth plan. So, I guess this is presented very much as like a replacement for the American Airlines portfolio in combination with General Motors. You've got the same kind of receivables target and talking about the profitability. I'm just curious, if you'd retained the American Airlines portfolio for example, would you still have done this transaction? How are you thinking about allocation to the business going forwards, where profitability has been strong this quarter.",
  "answer_quote": "Let's just step back a little bit and think about what Best Egg does for USCB. It creates scale and capability, and they are the things that we've talked about sort of repeatedly when we talked about potential acquisitions. So, the loss of American Airlines clearly gave us a question on scale, but the question of capability is somewhat beyond American Airlines. Clearly it's capital light revenue, but I think, you know, this is digital first, [has] superior risk capability in an area adjacent to what we already do. In fact, we are in this business in a small way. So, it's first and foremost a capability purchase, and we've been talking to the business for nine months. That's really what attracted us. Actually, the sort of to-ing and fro-ing in terms of scale, is somewhat an output. However, as you point out, we're essentially taking a relatively low risk adjusted margin, capital heavy source of revenue and replacing it with a capital light, high RoTE source of revenue. Growth from here, we clearly see growth in this particular business because there are potential revenue synergies there. I think that's not only from the Best Egg customers coming to us directly and us being able to sell cards and deposits to them. It's clearly in the opposite direction, being able to take that product into our full partner suite. We do it with about 10 partners at the moment to give you an idea, but it is small. And then there are clearly revenue synergies in respect to funding and also in securing our flow of ABS business, if you like, into the Investment Bank. So, all of these things are in our mind. That said, the core business and our focus on improving the profitability of the core business in USCB remains. So this is in no way a substitute for all of the stuff that we have been doing for a number of quarters now, in which you're seeing in the Q3 results and we would expect to replicate. But if the essence of your question is, should we expect to see a series of these in the US? The answer to that is no. Because essentially this is about, as I said, firmly a capability purchase. data.question_intent: Inquiries about USCB's capital allocation and growth plan, specifically regarding Best Egg and deposit business within BUK.
data.question_quote: Two questions from me. One again, just on Best Egg, but just more in terms of USCB capital allocation and growth plan. So, I guess this is presented very much as like a replacement for the American Airlines portfolio in combination with General Motors. You've got the same kind of receivables target and talking about the profitability. I'm just curious, if you'd retained the American Airlines portfolio for example, would you still have done this transaction? How are you thinking about allocation to the business going forwards, where profitability has been strong this quarter.
data.answer_quote: Let's just step back a little bit and think about what Best Egg does for USCB. It creates scale and capability, and they are the things that we've talked about sort of repeatedly when we talked about potential acquisitions. So, the loss of American Airlines clearly gave us a question on scale, but the question of capability is somewhat beyond American Airlines. Clearly it's capital light revenue, but I think, you know, this is digital first, [has] superior risk capability in an area adjacent to what we already do. In fact, we are in this business in a small way. So, it's first and foremost a capability purchase, and we've been talking to the business for nine months. That's really what attracted us. Actually, the sort of to-ing and fro-ing in terms of scale, is somewhat an output. However, as you point out, we're essentially taking a relatively low risk adjusted margin, capital heavy source of revenue and replacing it with a capital light, high RoTE source of revenue. Growth from here, we clearly see growth in this particular business because there are potential revenue synergies there. I think that's not only from the Best Egg customers coming to us directly and us being able to sell cards and deposits to them. It's clearly in the opposite direction, being able to take that product into our full partner suite. We do it with about 10 partners at the moment to give you an idea, but it is small. And then there are clearly revenue synergies in respect to funding and also in securing our flow of ABS business, if you like, into the Investment Bank. So, all of these things are in our mind. That said, the core business and our focus on improving the profitability of the core business in USCB remains. So this is in no way a substitute for all of the stuff that we have been doing for a number of quarters now, in which you're seeing in the Q3 results and we would expect to replicate. But if the essence of your question is, should we expect to see a series of these in the US? The answer to that is no. Because essentially this is about, as I said, firmly a capability purchase. And having got that capability, growth from here should be in scaling that business in a capital light way and in continuing to grow our US cards business very much in the way that you've seen us do it before, both organically and inorganically at the same kind of cadence.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the questions about USCB's capital allocation and growth plan, specifically regarding Best Egg and the deposit business within BUK, providing a detailed explanation and forward guidance, with high evidence level including numeric evidence and forward guidance.
